territorial_scope.description: Extends to England and Wales and applies to business or commercial projects under the Planning Act 2008 regime.

evidence.quote: These Regulations extend to England and Wales.

summary.short: Amends the Infrastructure Planning (Business or Commercial Projects) Regulations 2013 to add data centres to the prescribed description of business or commercial projects under the Planning Act 2008 regime in England and Wales, in force from 8 January 2026.
summary.long: The Regulations were made on 7 January 2026 and came into force on 8 January 2026. Regulation 2 inserts a new paragraph 10, 'Data centres', into the Schedule to the 2013 Regulations after paragraph 9 (Tourism), so that data centre projects fall within the prescribed description of business or commercial projects for the purposes of section 35(2)(a)(ii) of the Planning Act 2008. According to the Explanatory Note, development forming part of such a project can be authorised under the planning regime if other section 35 requirements are met and the Secretary of State gives a direction, which may be given only where the project is of national significance. The Regulations extend to England and Wales. They contain no other operative provisions, and no full impact assessment was produced.

relations.note: Made under the powers in sections 35(2)(a)(ii) and 232(3) of the Planning Act 2008. The preamble also recites section 232(7) (draft laid before and approved by each House). The Explanatory Note, which is not part of the Regulations, describes section 35 directions.

evidence.quote: in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 35(2)(a)(ii) and 232(3) of the Planning Act

notes: The header reads 'INFRASTRUCTURE PLANNING, ENGLAND', but Reg. 1(3) states that the Regulations extend to England and Wales. The instrument does not define 'data centres'; the inserted entry is the words 'Data centres.' only. Footnote numerals are merged into citations in the source text (e.g., '20132', '20081'); they are read here as 2013 and 2008. The Explanatory Note is not part of the Regulations and is not coded as operative text.
